items.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: The one on Earl Hines had a full page review by James Baldwin, but it still was the least seller you know.

ctx.x: We struggled along? Was it ever — was it a good way to make a living for you?

No. Oh no. Because, no I mean there’s not great money in it. Not in writing. Of the four worlds I did — The World of Duke Ellington was the only one that made any real money. Not that it’s any better than the other three, but the thing is that it has the bigger name to it. The one on Earl Hines had a full page review by James Baldwin, but it still was the least seller you know. No, if you were going to try to make a living in that field, that’s why so many of them end up working for record companies. But you’ve…

Let me ask you about when you came over to make those first records. Did you have the freedom to say, to pick the artist and say all right, I want to do Coleman Hawkins? Did you then let him pick the rhythm section?
